rgb: The scene is an outdoor stone-paved yard covered in rows of grey molded egg trays on the ground to the right and center, with a wheeled multi-tiered metal rack holding blue boards and trays to the left and a green building roughly 0.3 to 1.5 metres away in the foreground. Far out of reach at the bottom of the frame (about 3 to 5 metres below and in front of the viewpoint), the camera wearer holds a flat blue board carrying egg trays that is partly cropped by the lower frame edge. In the first frame, the wheeled rack is 3 to 5 metres to the left (partly out of view on the left edge), a person in a red shirt stands 0.5 to 1.5 metres ahead facing and looking away from the camera wearer and 3 to 5 metres out of reach of the rack, and a person in a black shirt stands 0.5 to 1.5 metres ahead and about 1.5 to 2 metres right of the person in red, bending over the ground trays facing right with a blue board in his hands. Across the second and third frames, the viewpoint turns right and tilts downward toward the ground trays 1 to 6 metres away, moving the rack and the person in red out of view to the left while leaving only the legs and board of the person in black briefly visible at the upper-left edge in frame two. In the fourth frame, the viewpoint pitches straight down to show the camera wearer's hands gripping the tray-laden blue board about 3 to 5 metres away above their feet and partially occluding the pavement below, before tilting back up and turning left in the fifth frame to show the held blue board now empty at the bottom-center while the person in black stands upright 0.5 to 1.5 metres ahead facing away from the camera wearer with a blue board in hand, slightly in front of and about 3 to 5 metres right of the person in red who also faces away from the camera wearer far from the rack.
depth: The depth map shows an open outdoor paved courtyard covered in rows of egg cartons on the right and a multi-tiered wheeled rack of blue boards on the left, with a blue board held far out of reach (~3–5 m) below the camera wearer's viewpoint across all five frames. In Frame 1, two workers stand ahead to the right of the rack—one in red upright at ~0.5–1.5 m facing away from the camera wearer and another in black bent over ~3–5 m to his right at ~0.5–1.5 m—before the wearer turns right and tilts downward across Frames 2–4 toward the ground (~1–2 m away) and then turns left in Frame 5 to face the rack (~3–5 m on the left) and the two workers (~0.5–1.5 m ahead, ~3–5 m apart, both facing away from the wearer with the worker in black holding a board that is out of his reach). In Frame 4, the bright foreground clearly separates the elevated blue board and cartons (~3–5 m) and the wearer's supporting left arm and partially occluded right hand from the darker ground and right foot (~3–5 m) directly below. Compared to RGB alone, the continuous luminance gradient makes the ground plane's recession and the vertical step between the held board and the floor immediately apparent even where repetitive carton textures flatten perspective. However, the map is unreliable on the thin metal frame of the rack, which merges into the foreground depth, and in Frame 4 where the ground appears abnormally dark relative to Frames 2 and 3 despite a similar viewing distance.
segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete foreground and background entities across the courtyard, detecting three people in Frame 1—the bent worker in black (~0.5–1.5 m, center-right), the standing worker in red (~0.5–1.5 m, center, ~3–5 m left of the first), and a tiny nearby figure (~0.5–1.5 m behind the first worker's shoulder)—while leaving the ground, egg cartons, and wheeled rack unsegmented. As the camera wearer turns right and looks down in Frame 2, only the lower legs of a person at the upper-left edge (~0.5–1.5 m away and within reach) remain in view, and Frame 3 is completely empty of masks as the viewpoint faces the ground grid of cartons (~3–5 m). In Frame 4, at far range (~3–5 m), the map segments the wearer's extended left arm on the lower left and right foot on the lower center as distinct person instances out of arm's reach, and in Frame 5 it re-detects the two upright workers side by side ~0.5–1.5 m ahead (~3–5 m apart, with the worker in black slightly farther and partly occluding the rack far from the worker in red). This map makes it easier than RGB alone to spot the tiny nearby person in Frame 1 and to separate the overlapping silhouettes of the two workers in Frame 5. However, it is highly unreliable for object classes and completeness, misclassifying two moulded egg cartons on the held board in Frame 4 as 'pizza' and a blue shelf on the rack in Frame 5 as 'boat', while failing to segment the wearer's partially occluded right hand in Frame 4 and all other boards and cartons.
pose: The pose map renders 2D skeletal keypoints on a black background, capturing only the upright worker in red in Frame 1 (~0.5–1.5 m ahead, right of the rack), the wearer's own left hand in Frame 4 (~3–5 m ahead, lower left), and the worker in black in Frame 5 (~0.5–1.5 m ahead, center-left). In Frame 1, the yellow body skeleton shows the worker in red standing in three-quarter profile facing away and slightly right with his head oriented away from the camera wearer and his arms hanging 3 to 5 metres out of reach of the distant rack, while the bent worker ~3–5 m to his right is completely missed. Frames 2 and 3 contain no skeletal detections at all because the person at the top-left of Frame 2 is mostly out of view above the knees and Frame 3 shows only the ground and the bottom edge of the held board. In Frame 4, a magenta hand skeleton highlights the curled fingers and thumb of the wearer's left hand gripping the bottom edge of the blue board far out of arm's reach, and in Frame 5 a yellow body skeleton shows the worker in black facing away from the camera wearer with both elbows bent and forearms raised to hold a board at chest height. While the skeletons clarify the exact finger articulation under the board edge in Frame 4 and limb joint positions in Frames 1 and 5 better than RGB alone, the map is unreliable because it misses the bent worker in Frame 1, the wearer's partially occluded right hand and foot in Frame 4, the second standing worker in Frame 5, and all hand skeletons on the nearby workers.
